newsitem.title: NORWAY: SAS could disappear in 5-10 years - report.
newsitem.headline: SAS could disappear in 5-10 years - report.

text.p: Scandinavian Airline Systems (SAS) could disappear as an independent airline company in the next five to 10 years, according to consultants Cap Gemini Group, the daily Aftenposten said on Tuesday.
SAS is not facing up to the demands of deregulation of the airline industry, increasing competition and lower prices, said Alun Evans, head of Cap Gemini's transport division.
"SAS is facing many challenges and I do not see how they are going to tackle them," Evans was quoted by Aftenposten as saying.

"Our assessment is that in the course of the next five to 10 years there will be four or five large groups in air travel. Companies such as SAS, Finnair, Sabena and other well-know airliners will simply no longer exist."
Evans said SAS required to undergo "dramatic" changes. The group's costs are substantially higher per seat per kilometer than, for example, British Airways or Lufthansa, he said.

He added that following deregulation of the industry in April there has been increasing opportunity for airlines to operate in other lands, and noted that both Virgin and Ryan Air were making moves into the Scandinavian market.
